la:noun:lax.html:
lax
cf. Gr. λέχρις; Lat.: licinus, luxus
,
fraud, deception: lacit decipiendo inducit. Lax etenim fraus est, Paul. ex .

la:verb:laxo.html:
laxo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. (rarely n.; v. I. B. 2. β. and II. B. β. infra) [id.],
to stretch out, extend, to make wide or roomy, to expand.
Lit.: forum,: manipulos,to open the ranks,: lilium ab angustiis in latitudinem paulatim se laxans,.—
Transf.
To open, undo, unloose (syn. solvo): vincula epistolae laxavit,: nodos Herculeos,: ubi dolor vocem laxaverat,had loosened his voice,: claustra,: claustra portarum,: intestina,.—
To slacken, relax: laxare arcum,to slacken, unbend,: excussos rudentes,: laxantur corpora rugis,become flabby with wrinkles,: laxatis habenis invehi jussit,; : laxatisque vinculis ... ostendit manum,: se cutis arida laxet,: oleum ad nervos laxandos utile est,: corpus velut laxatum,: ferrum,to smelt,.—
Neutr.: crebris fluctibus compages operis verberatae laxavere,were loosened, opened,.—
To lighten, ease: pharetra graves laxavit umeros,.—
Trop.
To lighten, relieve, unbend, recreate (syn.: levo, libero): a contentione disputationis animos curamque laxemus, : judicum animos atque a severitate ad hilaritatem traducere,: animum ab assiduis laboribus,: ut istis te molestiis laxes, release yourself, Luc. ap. .—
To relax, mitigate, moderate, abate, weaken: alicui laxare aliquid laboris,: vix primos inopina quies laxaverat artus,: placida laxarant membra quiete ... nautae,: subtile examen justitiae,: iram,: nigrantes tenebras : paulatim temeritate laxata,: longiore dierum spatio laxare dicendi necessitatem,to prolong, delay, defer,: memoriae inhaeret fldelius, quod nulla scribendi securitate laxatur,: rarescit multo laxatus vulnere miles,weakened,.—To lay open, disclose, reveal (poet.): fata latentia laxa,.—
To reduce the price of: annonam,; so neutr., to lessen, fall in price: annona laxaverat,.—laxātus, a, um, P. a., spread out, separated, extended, wide.
Lit.: custodiae,i. e. separated, withdrawn,: custodia,: membrana laxatior,: laxati ordines (aciei),; : corpore laxati,released from the body,—
Trop.: libidinum vinculis laxati,released, freed, free,: laxatus curis,: pugna,a battle broken off,: nox,i. e. clear,.

la:adj:laxus.html:
laxus, a, um, adj.
cf. languidus, languor, lactes
,
wide, loose, open; spacious, roomy; opp. adstrictus (not freq. till after the Aug. per.).
Lit.: laxius agmen, Sall. ap. : casses,: circli,: sinus,: toga,; ; cf.: in pede calceus haeret,wide, loose,: nuces Ferre sinu laxo,: qua satis laxo spatio equi permitti possent,; so, spatium,wide, roomy,; cf.: laxior domus,: janua,open,: compages,: mulier,: habenae, (v. under II.); : frena,; cf.: qui jam contento, jam laxo fune laborat,: arcus,slackened, unbent, unstrung,: laxo meditantur arcu cedere campis,: opes,large, great,.—
Trop.: laxissimas habenas habere amicitiae,very wide, loose,: si bellum cum eo hoste haberemus, in quo neglegentiae laxior locus esset, greater latitude or scope, ; cf.: laxius imperium,less strict, more indulgent,: annona,i. e. reduced, cheap,: caput,relaxed, disordered from drinking,: vox,pronounced broad,: laxioribus verbis dicere aliquid,prolix, diffuse,.—Of time: diem statuo satis laxam,sufficiently distant,: tempus sibi et quidem laxius postulavit,—Hence, adv.: laxē, widely, spaciously, loosely.
Lit.: vis sideris laxe grassantis,: distans,: aurum laxius dilatatur,: Mercurii stella laxissime vagatur,: medio suspendit vincula ponto, Et laxe fluitare sinit,loosely, freely,: manus vincire,loosely,.—
Trop.: laxius proferre diem,to put farther off,; cf.: volo laxius (sc. rem curari),: de munere pastorum alii angustius, alii laxius constituere solent,a greater number, more,: in hostico laxius rapto suetis vivere artiores in pace res erant,more unrestrictedly, more freely,: Romanos remoto metu laxius licentiusque futuros,be more relaxed in discipline, more negligent, disorderly,.

la:noun:laxamentum.html:
laxāmentum, i, n.
laxo
,
an extending, widening.
Lit. (post-Aug.): ventus laxamentum sibi parat,: cellae,: ventris,an evacuating, purging,.—
Transf. (in concr.), a wide space, room: choragia laxamentum habeant, ad chorum parandum,.—
Trop., a relaxation, mitigation, alleviation, respite (not freq. till after the Aug. per.): si quid laxamenti a bello Samnitium esset,: eo laxamento cogitationibus dato,: ut minus laxamenti daretur iis ad auxilia Hannibali submittenda,; : nactus in navigatione pusillum laxamenti, Trebon. ap. : dare laxamentum legi,laxity, indulgence,; so, leges rem surdam, inexorabilem esse ... nihil laxamenti nec veniae habere,.

laxus
